Fig. 6
Formation of desmosine and its isomer isodesmosine from lysine residues in human collagen and elastin for intramolecular and
intermolecular cross links. Lysyl oxidase [an ascorbate (Asc, vitamin C) and copper-dependent enzyme] catalyzes the oxidative deamination of lysine
residue into allysine residue. Condensations between the indicated molecules occur as spontaneous reactions (SRN) to form desmosine and
isodesmosine, which consist of 4 lysine residues to form a pyridinium nucleus. Substrates and products, which are residues in collagen and elastin
of all the reactions, are shown. In their intact molecules and non-ionized form, the “–HCO–” group is “–HCOOH” and the “–NH–” group should be
“–NH2”. The molecular formula of intact desmosine and isodesmosine is C24H40N5O8 (MW ¼ 526.603).

Solubility of AAs in water and organic solvents
All AAs are soluble in water. Leucine, isoleucine, valine, phenylalanine, tryptophan, methionine, tyrosine, and cysteine are among
the most hydrophobic AAs. Proline and cystine are the most and least soluble, respectively (Table 3). The solubility of tyrosine in
